newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks rise on CANTV sale details.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks rise on CANTV sale details.

text.p: Caracas stocks firmed on news that the global share offering of the government's 40 percent share in telephone company CANTV would take place in the last week of November, traders said.
"CANTV's imminent sale is definitely bringing back confidence to the market," said Amerival broker Juan Domingo Perez.
The bolsa's 19-share .IBC index gained 0.62 percent to close at 5,998.36 points as nearly 26 million shares traded worth 3.6 billion bolivars ($7.7 million).

Financial daily Economia Hoy reported the share offering would begin November 22, while trading in the new issue on the Caracas stock exchange would start November 26. The share price was reported at an estimated $3.25.
"Everyone's hoping to get in on early buys of the stock which, from international experience, usually gives back a good return," Perez added.

Among traded issues, 24 rose, 11 closed flat and eight fell. Market leader Electricidad de Caracas gained 12.50 bolivars to close at 539.00 bolivars, while Mavesa rose 2.50 bolivars to end at 155.00 bolivars.
Traders saw the bourse's gentle rise continuing, with continued exchange rate stability helping maintain market tone.
